subject: Animation
title: Lotte Reiniger: Silhouette Cinema Pioneer
description: A fast breakdown of Lotte Reiniger: Silhouette Cinema Pioneer for builders.

hook.text: In 1926, Lotte Reiniger completed The Adventures of Prince Achmed, arguably the first animated feature film.

buildup.text: Reiniger used silhouette cutout animation — articulated paper figures filmed against backlit colored screens.

discovery.text: The film predates Disney's Snow White by eleven years, challenging who truly made the first animated feature.

twist.text: Reiniger was a German Jewish artist who fled the Nazis. Her early works were nearly destroyed during World War II.

climax.text: Reiniger made over 40 films across six decades, yet most animation histories barely mention her name.

punchline.text: The first feature filmmaker in animation was a woman most people forgot.

quiz.question: What is Lotte Reiniger's claim to animation history?
options: She created the first color animated short
She directed The Adventures of Prince Achmed in 1926, arguably the first animated feature film
She invented the cel animation process

details.summary: Lotte Reiniger created The Adventures of Prince Achmed in 1926, the oldest surviving animated feature film. Her intricate silhouette animation, cut from black cardboard and lit from behind, produced mesmerizing stories drawn from A Thousand and One Nights.
details.whyItMatters: Reiniger proved feature-length animation was possible a decade before Snow White. Her silhouette technique created a visual language so distinctive that it continues to influence paper-cut and shadow animation today.
takeaways: Prince Achmed in 1926 is the oldest surviving animated feature film
Reiniger's silhouette technique used articulated cardboard figures on glass
She produced over 40 animated films across six decades

faq.question: How did Reiniger create her silhouette animations?
faq.answer: She cut articulated figures from black cardboard, arranged them on illuminated glass plates, and photographed them frame by frame. The resulting silhouettes moved with remarkable fluidity and expressiveness despite their apparent simplicity.

faq.question: Why is Reiniger often overlooked in animation history?
faq.answer: As a woman working in early 20th-century Germany, her work was marginalized by wartime disruption and an industry that privileged male American and Japanese creators. Recent scholarship has re-established her as one of animation's most important pioneers.
